source_caption:
To perfectly physicalize the fiercely unrelenting, deeply unapologetic rage of a grieving mother demanding answers, Frances McDormand made a wildly brilliant, highly specific wardrobe decision for her character, Mildred Hayes. She completely rejected the idea of traditional costume changes, insisting that Mildred wear the exact same dark blue, heavily utilitarian mechanic’s jumpsuit in almost every single scene, treating it entirely as an armor-plated uniform of war. Drawing profound inspiration from the fiercely stoic, heavily iconic performances of John Wayne, McDormand completely stripped away any traditional vanity or softness from the role. By stubbornly refusing to change out of her intensely practical, deeply stained coveralls, McDormand masterfully proves that the most devastatingly powerful cinematic protagonists don’t need sprawling wardrobes—they just need an unwavering, fiercely terrifying visual statement of absolute battle readiness.
⠀
Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (2017), directed by Martin McDonagh, starring Frances McDormand, Woody Harrelson, Sam Rockwell. A fiercely furious, profoundly grieving mother completely loses her patience with the heavily incompetent local police force, renting three massive, deeply provocative billboards to publicly shame the wildly respected police chief into finally solving her daughter’s fiercely brutal, completely unsolved murder.

source_details.synopsis: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri is a 2017 British dark comedy crime film written, directed, and produced by Martin McDonagh. It stars Frances McDormand as Mildred Hayes, a Missouri woman who rents three roadside billboards to draw attention to her daughter's unsolved rape and murder. Woody Harrelson, Sam Rockwell, Abbie Cornish, John Hawkes, and Peter Dinklage appear in supporting roles. The film was theatrically released in the United States in November 2017 and in the United Kingdom in January 2018 by Fox Searchlight Pictures, and it grossed $162 million at the worldwide box office.
